steps.say: Some babies cannot be oxygenated no matter how hard the ventilator works. The heart lung machine takes over outside the body, adding oxygen, removing carbon dioxide and pumping blood around the failing heart and lungs. It buys days for the underlying disease to turn around. It takes over when ventilators and drugs can no longer keep oxygen up.
steps.tx: **Extracorporeal membrane oxygenation** (heart-lung bypass) gives temporary cardiopulmonary support with **carbon dioxide removal** (waste-gas clearance), **oxygenation** (oxygen loading) and **circulatory support** (pump-assisted flow) for refractory respiratory or cardiac failure, **sepsis** (bloodstream infection) and extracorporeal resuscitation. It serves refractory failure when **ventilators** (breathing machines) and drugs cannot sustain gas exchange.

steps.say: The commonest reason a newborn goes on the machine is lungs clogged with the first stool. These babies turn pink on bypass more than nine times out of ten, recovering quickly. Breathing distress of prematurity, persistent high lung pressure, bloodstream infection and hernia of the diaphragm fill the remaining beds.
steps.tx: **Meconium aspiration** (first-stool lungs) is the most common neonatal indication with survival above **90** (ninety) percent, alongside **respiratory distress syndrome** (premature stiff lungs), **persistent pulmonary hypertension** (locked lung pressure), sepsis and congenital diaphragmatic hernia (hole in diaphragm). These are **neonatal ECMO** (newborn bypass) indications. Reversible disease predicts success.

steps.say: The circuit looks complex but each part has one job. A tube drains dark blood from a great vein, the pump pushes it forward, the membrane lung adds oxygen and takes carbon dioxide, the warmer holds temperature, and a second tube returns bright blood to the body. The diagram traces this loop, showing each part.
steps.tx: The **circuit** (tubing loop) drains venous blood through a **cannula** (access tube), drives it with a **pump** (flow generator) across a membrane **oxygenator** (artificial lung) that loads oxygen and strips **carbon dioxide** (waste gas), then returns oxygenated blood. The **reservoir** (blood chamber) and warmer stabilise volume and temperature.

vis.alt: Diagram of cardiopulmonary bypass circuit with cannulated heart, reservoir, pump and oxygenator.
vis.caption: Cannula, reservoir, pump and oxygenator in the extracorporeal loop. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: The machine is offered when death is otherwise likely. A gradient above six hundred ten for many hours, or above six hundred twenty for six hours with air leak and low pressure, or an oxygen index above forty all mark eighty percent predicted mortality without support.
steps.tx: **ECMO** (bypass support) is indicated near **80** (eighty) percent **predicted mortality** (expected death rate), with an **alveolar arterial gradient** (lung oxygen gap) above **610** (six hundred ten) for **8** (eight) to **12** (twelve) hours or above **620** (six hundred twenty) for **6** (six) hours with **barotrauma** (pressure injury) and hypotension.

steps.say: One number combines ventilator pressure and blood oxygen to guide the decision. Multiply the oxygen fraction by the mean airway pressure and a hundred, then divide by the arterial oxygen. Crossing forty means four out of five babies die without the machine. The number blends ventilator pressure with blood blueness, combining both sides.
steps.tx: The **oxygen index** (failure score) equals inspired **oxygen fraction** (oxygen dial) times **mean airway pressure** (average ventilator push) times **100** (one hundred) divided by arterial **oxygen** (blood oxygen). Values above **40** (forty) predict **80** (eighty) percent mortality without bypass. Mean airway pressure reflects **ventilator intensity** (support level), so the index blends support level with oxygenation.

steps.say: Not every baby can safely go on bypass. Extreme prematurity threatens brain bleeding, weight under two kilograms makes cannulation unsafe, existing brain bleed forbids blood thinners, and irreversible lung disease or lethal syndromes make support futile. Each contraindication is checked before cannulation.
steps.tx: **Contraindications** (bypass bans) are severe **prematurity** (early-gestation risk) with **intracranial bleed** (brain bleeding) risk, weight under **2** (two) kg, existing intracranial bleed, irreversible lung disease like **alveolar dysplasia** (hopeless lung growth failure), **cyanotic heart disease** (blue-heart lesion) and intractable **coagulopathy** (unclottable blood).

steps.say: In small children the neck vessels carry the circuit. The vein and the artery on one side of the neck are joined to the machine, and the artery is usually tied off when the tubes come out, which babies tolerate well. Older children use the groin vessels with an extra small tube keeping the leg alive.
steps.tx: **Venoarterial ECMO** (vein-to-artery bypass) cannulation uses the right **internal jugular vein** (neck vein) and **common carotid artery** (neck artery) in young children, the carotid usually undergoes **carotid ligation** (artery tie-off) at **decannulation** (tube removal) which babies tolerate, and older children use **femoral cannulation** (groin-vessel access) with a distal **perfusion cannula** (leg-flow tube). **Venovenous ECMO** (vein-to-vein bypass) suits isolated lung failure through one neck vein.

steps.say: Injured lungs pass through recognisable stages that the picture lays out. First the air sacs flood and stiffen, then scar tissue fills them, and finally the architecture distorts permanently. Bypass offered before the scarring stage lets the lungs rest while the exudative injury heals.
steps.tx: **ARDS** (acute lung injury) moves through exudative flooding, proliferative scarring and fibrotic distortion of the **alveoli** (air sacs). **Venovenous bypass** (vein-to-vein support) with a **double lumen cannula** (two-channel tube) suits respiratory failure with good cardiac function, restoring stability through well oxygenated blood.

vis.alt: Sequential diagram of acute lung injury through exudative, proliferative and fibrotic phases.
vis.caption: Exudative, proliferative and fibrotic phases of acute lung injury. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: Bleeding is the price of the circuit. Cannula sites, chest and brain can all bleed on blood thinners, and babies under thirty four weeks bleed into the brain most often. Recovery shows as rising oxygen, softer lungs and a clearing film before the team clamps the circuit for a trial.
steps.tx: **Bleeding** (circuit cost) is the most common complication at cannula, thoracic and intracranial sites, and gestation under **34** (thirty four) weeks best predicts **intracranial hemorrhage** (brain bleed), with recovery shown by rising arterial oxygen, better compliance and clearing radiograph before clamp trial, the markers of **lung recovery** (healing lungs).
